$comment: Field-guide metadata for the documentation site. Keyed by plugin name; every plugins/<name>/plugin.json must have an entry here and vice versa (tests/test_field_guide.py). use_when and try open each plugin page and the homepage key; try must be an invocation the plugin's entry accepts. Habitat, diet, and field marks are reviewed by hand against the plugin's entry.md.

imps.summary: Fix a bug or implement a change, with checks and review tied to the files you receive.
imps.use_when: You can name the failure and what fixed looks like, and you want the checks that prove it run against the files you get back.
imps.try: $t3-imps run fix the date parser: reject 31 April with a clear error, add a regression test, do not commit
imps.habitat: A T3 thread attached to a repository, with a small Python core holding run state.
imps.diet: One task with observable acceptance criteria and an agreed Open PR, Tagged Version or Verified in Prod target.
imps.field_marks: Any edit after verification makes the evidence stale. Blocked is a complete answer. Delegation goes through T3 only.

ape.summary: Find an approach in another codebase, with source citations and a small experiment to try.
ape.use_when: Another project has probably solved your problem, and you want its code cited by line before you borrow the idea.
ape.try: $t3-ape https://github.com/python/cpython how are parser error cases tested?
ape.habitat: A research workspace of cloned repositories, outside your project.
ape.diet: A named gap and a GitHub search, or one repository URL.
ape.field_marks: Read-only in the current project. Every recommendation cites source lines and proposes a small experiment. Never runs third-party code.

babysitter.summary: Carry an authorized PR through review, failing checks and conflicts to an observed merge.
babysitter.use_when: A pull request is stuck on review comments, red checks or conflicts, and you want it fixed and watched until it merges.
babysitter.try: $t3-babysitter pr https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/12 inspect reviews and CI only
babysitter.habitat: One pull request, a repository, or an organization, within the scope you state.
babysitter.diet: Review findings, red checks, and base-branch drift.
babysitter.field_marks: "Review" alone authorizes inspection only. Pushes to the PR branch only. Never bypasses protected-branch rules. T3 owns the watch.

agent-tuneup.summary: Check all agent wiring, inspect available usage and prepare approved native changes.
agent-tuneup.use_when: You want to check shared instructions, skills, permissions, MCPs, roles and repository setup across your T3 providers.
agent-tuneup.habitat: A T3 thread with a live provider catalog and identified configuration sources.
agent-tuneup.diet: A complete wiring audit, a narrower explicit target, or approval of concrete changes.
agent-tuneup.field_marks: One workflow covers readiness, audit, usage analysis, alignment and approved apply. Settings writes require a concrete reviewed plan and private backup.

ralph.summary: Implement a goal and repair independent evaluator findings through the agreed delivery target.
ralph.use_when: You want one model to implement a goal and a model from another lineage to grade it, with every criticism sent back for another attempt.
ralph.try: $t3-ralph fix the parser and add regression coverage
ralph.habitat: One T3 parent thread and a retained worktree, with checkpoints outside the repository.
ralph.diet: A goal, exact work and reviewer backup chains, and a retained attempt limit.
ralph.field_marks: Fresh review tasks. All feedback triggers repair. Retained budgets. Completion requires Open PR, Tagged Version or Verified in Prod evidence.

focus-group.summary: Test a product with an editable panel of invented personas across several models.
focus-group.use_when: You want to know what to fix, build and keep in a product or prototype, and you will treat the answers as hypotheses rather than customer evidence.
focus-group.try: $t3-focus-group plan https://staging.example/welcome first-run experience for busy parents
focus-group.habitat: A T3 thread with a live model catalog, a private study directory and shared captures of the product.
focus-group.diet: An audience, a decision to inform, a target or capture pack, and an approved panel and task ceiling.
focus-group.field_marks: Planning reviews the study before panel work. Every revision is approved by hash. Unknown capabilities stay unknown until a pilot. Results are synthetic hypotheses, never demand.

bug-report.summary: Verify upstream defects, use their documented reporting method and follow up for 30 minutes.
bug-report.use_when: An upstream project or service appears broken and you want evidence and a report through its known reporting channel.
bug-report.habitat: A T3 conversation, a private reporting ledger and a separate reporting thread.
bug-report.diet: A symptom or relevant conversation context, observed evidence and current report destinations.
bug-report.field_marks: Unknown reporting methods retain a private draft. Verified upstreams use their documented channel. Follow-up retains one fixed deadline.

plan.summary: Turn an uncertain problem into a reviewed, testable plan and a handoff.
plan.use_when: You know something should change and want to establish the problem, decisions and observable acceptance before implementation.
plan.habitat: A plans directory inside your repository.
plan.diet: A problem you cannot yet state as a task.
plan.field_marks: Planning ends at the handoff. Source review binds the exact discovery, specification and declared evidence.

tests-omg.summary: Inspect test protection and validation cost, with private HTML and evidence-based recommendations.
tests-omg.use_when: Validation is slow and you want to know what protection each check adds before simplifying the suite.
tests-omg.habitat: An attached repository or a bounded visible organization inventory.
tests-omg.diet: Source, existing runner outputs, incident history and explicitly authorized local measurements.
tests-omg.field_marks: Advisory and read-only by default. Twelve findings keep unknowns visible. No CI changes or report publication.
